title: Keratocyte fragments migrate to the anode while whole keratocytes migrate to the cathode

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Keratocyte fragments migrate to the anode while whole keratocytes migrate to the cathode

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In an electric field, whole keratocytes migrate toward the cathode while fragments of keratocytes migrate toward the anode, so the collective (an intact cell) has the opposite taxis to its parts, illustrating that collective behaviour can be a hard-to-predict function of component tendencies.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: McMillen P 2024, Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates › Introduction › Cell migration: the group does not go where each of the parts wants to go

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: In an electric field, keratocytes migrate to the cathode, but fragments of keratocytes migrate to the anode104.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: McMillen P, Levin M, “Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates”, Communications biology (2024), doi:10.1038/s42003-024-06037-4; section “Introduction › Cell migration: the group does not go where each of the parts wants to go”. Scope: Fish keratocytes and keratocyte fragments in applied electric fields

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2024-collective-04: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.70

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Direction relative to electrode polarity is an unusually clean and decisive readout. Published data can check the reversal, though mechanistic conclusions about whole-versus-part tendencies remain less resolved.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Calculate signed migration velocities of intact keratocytes and matched fragments under identical electric-field polarity, strength, and medium conditions.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Fragment production may alter polarity machinery as well as collectivity.

Raw trajectories from the cited experiment may not be deposited.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.52
analysis feasibility: 0.78
discriminating power: 0.9
operationalizability: 0.98
data adequacy: 0.4

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Direction relative to a defined field, with reversal controls, is a clean contrast, and the primary paper publishes trajectories, summary directedness and movies for both cells and fragments. That is scattered published measurement rather than an open tracking archive a third party can download and rerun. The opposite-taxis result can be re-measured from those materials with real limits on precision, which is a partial rather than a complete resolution.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In the same electric-field polarity, compute directedness of intact fish keratocytes and of their anucleate fragments, including field-reversal trials. Cathodal cells and anodal fragments, both reversing when the field reverses, would support opposite taxis; the same direction for fragments and cells would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Retyping trajectories from figures is less precise than the original tracking files.

Raw tracks are in the paper and supplement, not a separate downloadable coordinate archive.

The result is for fish keratocytes, which is the claim's scope, but fragment preparation can select a biased subset of cytoplasm.

fields.label: Hypothesis
fields.value: In published measurements of fish keratocytes in a direct-current electric field, intact cells move toward the cathode (positive directedness, cos theta > 0 with the cathode at 0 degrees) and cell fragments in the same field conditions move toward the anode (negative directedness).

fields.label: Method
fields.value: analysis.py downloads the Sun et al. 2013 supplement, checks its SHA-256, extracts the text of its compressed PDF streams with the standard library and confirms that all 20 transcribed 'mean ± SE' directedness values of Table S1 (field-strength series 0-6 V/cm plus the 4 V/cm DMSO and pH 7.4 controls) occur in it. For each field strength it computes a one-sample z = mean/SE for cells and fragments and applies the pre-registered thresholds (cells >= +0.5, fragments <= -0.3, both p < 0.01), with the fail rule checked at 4 and 6 V/cm, the strengths of the paper's main experiments (Figure 1 is at 6 V/cm).

fields.label: Pass criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered: in the published primary measurements (Sun et al. 2013, Current Biology, doi:10.1016/j.cub.2013.02.026, or other published measurements of fish keratocytes and their fragments), at the same field strength (a) the mean directedness of intact cells is >= +0.5 and (b) the mean directedness of fragments is <= -0.3, with each mean differing from 0 at p < 0.01 (one-sample test from the reported mean, dispersion and n; if only a mean and n are reported, a sign test on n is not possible and (a)/(b) must instead be supported by a reported test of the authors).

fields.label: Fail criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered: fragments have mean directedness >= 0 (no anodal migration) or intact cells have mean directedness <= 0 in the published measurements. Means in the right direction but below the magnitude thresholds or without p < 0.01 are pre-registered as 'mixed'. If no published numbers for both cells and fragments can be retrieved, the verdict is 'inconclusive' (data-unavailable).

fields.label: Unit
fields.value: mean directedness (cos angle to field, + = cathode) of keratocytes and fragments at 6 V/cm (Figure 1 conditions)

fields.label: Interpretation
fields.value: Taxis direction is measured as directedness, the mean cosine of the angle between each cell's net displacement and the field vector pointing to the cathode (+1 = straight to cathode, -1 = straight to anode), as is standard in electrotaxis studies. 'Fragments' are anucleate lamellipodial fragments of the same keratocytes. The claim's source is Levin's 2024 review, which cites the primary experiment rather than reporting data, so the primary publication by a different group (Zhao and Mogilner labs) is an admissible published measurement; it is the same experiment the claim rests on, not an independent replication. The claim's interpretive part (the collective has the opposite taxis to its parts, illustrating hard-to-predict collective behaviour) is not tested beyond the sign reversal.

fields.label: Datasets
fields.value: Sun et al. 2013, Current Biology 23:569-574, Supplemental Information (Table S1: directedness and speed of keratocytes and fragments under various EF conditions)

fields.label: Caveats
fields.value:
The sign reversal is large and clean at the paper's working field strengths: at 6 V/cm cells average +0.77 (n = 39) and fragments -0.59 (n = 151), at 4 V/cm +0.81 and -0.65, all |z| > 5; the vehicle and pH 7.4 controls at 4 V/cm repeat it. Cells are positive and fragments negative at every field from 0.5 V/cm up.

Not an independent replication: this is the primary experiment the review cites (a different lab from Levin's, so independent of the claim's author, but the same data). Table S1 is labelled 'data from a representative experiment', so n counts cells within one experiment, not independent experiments.

The pre-registration said 'at the same field strength' without naming one; the rule was applied to every strength and is met at 4 and 6 V/cm, the strengths of the main figures. Below 2 V/cm cell directedness is weak (<= 0.2), so 'whole keratocytes migrate to the cathode' holds for fields of a few V/cm, not for every field.

Without a field, fragments show a slight anodal bias (-0.13 ± 0.05, z = -2.6), which is small compared with -0.59 at 6 V/cm.

z tests use the reported SE and treat cells as independent; raw trajectories are not deposited, so the summary statistics could not be recomputed from tracks.

Only the directional claim is tested; the interpretation that this illustrates hard-to-predict collective behaviour is not a measurable quantity here.
